Note::strip¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note::strip() const -> Note
Note::strip(std::string_view chars) const -> Note

What It Does¶

Removes boundary characters from each text cell.

This method has two common modes:

  • plain whitespace trimming

  • explicit trimming of a chosen set of boundary characters

That makes it one of the core cleanup primitives in the Note surface.

The method is intentionally conservative: it only trims the left and right edges of each cell. Interior characters are left untouched.

Parameters¶

chars

Optional set of characters to trim from both ends of each cell.

  • strip() Uses the default whitespace-trimming behavior. This is the overload you want for ordinary cleanup of copied text, identifiers with padding, and cells that arrived from CSV or spreadsheet imports with accidental leading or trailing spaces or tabs.

  • strip(chars) Uses an explicit boundary character set instead of default whitespace. Every character present in chars is eligible for removal from the left boundary, the right boundary, or both, until a non-matching boundary character is reached.

This is boundary trimming only. Interior occurrences are untouched.

Returns¶

Note A new Note with the same shape as the input and trimmed boundaries.

Examples¶

Example 1. Remove leading and trailing whitespace.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"  Ada Lovelace  ", "\tGRACE HOPPER\t", "Linus"});
auto out = note.strip();
std::cout << "strip:\n" << out << "\n";

Output¶

strip:
  [0] Ada Lovelace
  [1] GRACE HOPPER
  [2] Linus

Example 2. Trim a custom boundary character set instead of whitespace.

auto tagged = pluss::make_note({"##alpha##", "#beta", "gamma##"});
auto out = tagged.strip("#");
std::cout << "strip_hash_space:\n" << pluss::print_note(out) << "\n";

Output¶

strip_hash_space:
  [0] alpha
  [1] beta
  [2] gamma

Example 3. Interior matches are preserved because strip() is a boundary operation, not a global deletion operation.

auto note = pluss::make_note({"#alpha#beta#", "##gamma##"});
auto trimmed = note.strip("#");
pluss::OutputEngine out;
out.writeln("strip_boundary_only:");
out.writeln(trimmed);

Output¶

strip_boundary_only:
  [0] alpha#beta
  [1] gamma

Notes¶

  • strip() preserves shape.

  • strip(chars) does not touch interior matches. It only trims the outer boundary runs.

  • This method is frequently paired with lower for standardized text normalization.

See Also¶

  • Note::lower: normalize case after trimming.

  • Note::replace: rewrite interior substrings rather than trimming boundaries.
